notes: Court-code fields are not uniform across Massachusetts Trial Court departments. This crosswalk documents the current MassCourts case-number code system separately from Tyler/EFSP route keys and from legacy Trial Court location codes.

District Court.meaning: Two-digit MassCourts site code used in District Court docket numbers.
District Court.status: current format page agrees with MACourts values; retired sites may retain historical codes. Winchendon 70 is historical after consolidation into Gardner 63.
District Court.tyler_code_meaning: Tyler Odyssey/EFM court location numeric route key (e.g. 438 for Attleboro, 672 for Worcester).

Boston Municipal Court.meaning: Two-digit MassCourts site code used in BMC docket numbers.

Housing Court.meaning: Division-level MassCourts code. Multiple physical sessions share one division code.
Housing Court.important: Stoughton, Canton, and Brockton are physical Metro South sessions and use H82 for MassCourts docket identity. Filings for Stoughton route to Canton (1265).

Superior Court.meaning: County-level MassCourts code. Multiple physical sessions within a county share the county code.

Probate and Family Court.record_field_meaning: Legacy Trial Court location code (P72-P85) retained for compatibility; this is not the site prefix used in current Probate docket numbers.
Probate and Family Court.current_masscourts_meaning: Two-letter site prefix at the start of a Probate and Family Court docket number.

Land Court.meaning: Land Court docket numbers do not contain a court-location code; they use year + case type + sequence.

Juvenile Court.meaning: Trial Court Juvenile location code. The consolidated 2021 registry contains historical/alternate codes as well as current physical-site identities.
Juvenile Court.important: Springfield appears under both J23 and J69 in the published registry. MACourts keeps one physical Springfield record, uses J69 as primary, and preserves J23 as an alias rather than creating two court locations.
Juvenile Court.tyler_code_notes: Tyler uses county-session codes (e.g. 1086:BO for Boston, 885:DE for Dedham). In Prod, 3-digit county prefixes lack leading zeroes (e.g. 705:LA), whereas in Dev/Test they are zero-padded to 4 digits (e.g. 0705:LA). Dudley 915:DU lacks leading zeroes in both environments.
